description.narrative:
The 2024 Africa Climate Caravan seeks to broaden and strengthen the climate justice movement across Africa, by supporting the mobilization of civil society movements, impacted communities, and citizens around the caravan's demands to local and national decision-makers for compliance with commitments made at previous COPs, in particular on the energy transition agreement to triple renewable energy capacity and double global energy efficiency by 2030, the phasing-out of fossil fuels, the raising of the future NDCs’ ambitions. The Africa Climate Caravan will also engage and influence local and national decision-makers to advocate for their populations needs and interests in regional and global spaces of climate diplomacy, especially on the climate finance needs for implementation of the loss and damage fund, the reach of the $100 million and the doubling of funds dedicated to communities’ adaptation needs. This is where the Oxfam’s confederation Make polluters pay Campaign messages will be integrated into the Climate Caravan call on governments and world leaders to tax the richest polluters and use that money to support those communities most impacted by the climate crisis and cover the costs of building a fairer future.
About the caravan in Senegal
Climate Caravan in Senegal will take place in October 2024, with a launch on Tuesday 15 October in Bargny, followed by a tour from 16 to 29 October in Ziguinchor, Kédougou, Podor andthe Saloum Delta. See detailed action plan.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam is working in Senegal since 1981 and has opened a first office in Senegal in 1983. Oxfam in Senegal is implementing a 5-year country strategy (2015-2019) which is articulated around the following vision which is:
Senegal has an active citizenry,comprising of a good representation of men, women and youth, that is willing and capable of influencing the development and implementation of national policies, and receives a more equitable share of the national wealth.
The country strategy uses a two-tiered approach: - to promote citizen participation in policy formulation and implementation processes; - To promote innovativefield programming that addresses the immediate needs of the poorest segments of society while strengthening their capacity to influence local authorities.
This strategy focusses on sustainable livelihoods, promoting good governance and humanitarian (contributingto strengthening the leadership of local actors in the context of integrated disaster management, from prevention to emergency response). It also recognizes the under-utilized potentialities and power of some marginalized groups, especially women and youth.
Oxfam in Senegal adheres to six partnership principles: shared vision and values,mutual accountability, complementarity, clarity of roles, institutional autonomy, and commitment to joint learning, and is carrying out projects through partnering with local NGOs and organisations (such as producer#s organisations).
